english.title: Licence holder / person restricted by licence of multi occupation house fail to comply with licence conditions
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), being a

(A)_[licence holder,]_
(B)_[person on whom restrictions or obligations under a licence were imposed in accordance with section 67(5) of the Housing Act 2004,]_

failed to comply with a condition of that licence in that **(..SPECIFY FAILURE..)
english.legislation: Contrary to section 72(3) and (7) of the Housing Act 2004.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location
licence holder / a person on whom restrictions / obligations under a licence were imposed
failed to comply with a condition of the licence.

investigatoraction.description: Guilty Plea by letter procedure may be offered for this offence
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes: In proceedings against a person for an offence under section 72(2), it is a defence from the 1st May 2026 that they had a reasonable excuse for permitting the person to occupy the house or for failing to comply with the condition as the case may be, under section 72(5).
english.standardstatementoffacts:

failed to comply with a condition of that licence in that **(..SPECIFY FAILURE..).

other.penalty:
Summary: A fine not exceeding level five on the standard scale.

Time limit for prosecutions:
6 months

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates' court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
